key_insight: Euler shifts AI math research from only producing final answers to supporting a shared, human-readable research graph that captures assumptions, proofs, failed attempts, and verification evidence.
engineering_relevance: For theorem proving systems, this provides persistent context across sessions so multi-agent workflows can plan, collaborate, and verify more reliably over long investigations.
method: Builds connected research graphs of mathematical statements, assumptions, dependencies, alternatives, failures, and evidence.
Lets researchers jump back to saved team states, inspect prior reasoning, and continue exploring from any graph node.
Uses the graph as shared memory for agent planning, collaboration, and verification across sessions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three mathematical research case studies plus an implemented system and software validation, but does not provide quantitative benchmark results.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify scalability, robustness against graph inconsistency, or how well the system handles very large or noisy multi-agent proof sessions.
paper_title: Euler: Towards Human-Centered Multi-Agent Mathematical Discovery
